title: list.append()
summary: Add a single object to the end of the list, in place.
description: Appends one item, whatever it is. Appending a list adds that list as a single element — use `extend` to add its contents instead.
returns: None — the list is modified in place.
real_world_usage: The standard way to build a list in a loop. When the loop only maps or filters, a comprehension is clearer and faster.

common_mistakes.fix: append returns None; you have just replaced your list with None.

common_mistakes.mistake: Using append when you meant extend
common_mistakes.fix: append adds one element; extend adds each element of an iterable.

performance_notes: Amortised O(1). CPython over-allocates, so most appends do not reallocate. Appending a million items is fine; `insert(0, x)` a million times is O(n²) — use collections.deque.
